The Arrow of Time

I figured I would use this space to jot down some of my ideas on time. At a glance, my take on the theory of everything is that we’re going to figure out these two things: 1) the master equation, and 2) the fundamental constants. If you feed these fundamental constants into that master equation, well, that is what we call the universe. The multiverse, on the other hand, is all possible permutations of this concept, which is spread out over a multidimensional space, all using a form of this same overarching equation, just with different fundamental constants based upon different coordinates in the multiverse. I originally wrote about this idea here. I also added a bit more to it here, in which I included the concept of a time-object which is fueling these constants of our universe, sort of like tidal-forces on Earth.

Another idea I had, was what if we threw out the distinction between space and time altogether, and just imagined that these were in fact two forms of the same kind of quantity, which I will refer to here as Ambul. What we have come to call time, is just another Ambul, but instead measuring our flow through this higher dimensional Ambul space. So, rather than thinking of it like three dimensions of space and one dimension of time, let’s call it four dimensions of Ambul. The reason something like a meter and a second are distinct, is not because of some inherent difference in quantity, but rather because we do not yet know enough about the multiverse to describe a second in terms of a meter.

Obviously, our location in Ambul space from one second to the next is different, and so we have defined a second as that Ambul displacement perpendicular to our direction of travel. This also implies that the universe one Ambul behind us is still totally just as valid as the one we are currently occupying, it’s just that we are now away from it. In other words, every moment exists at once just as every permutation does. It is all laid out in this crazy grid somewhere, and what we have falsely come to think of as progress is simply the displacement in this Ambul space – but specifically in this single orientation of “time”.

So the question is, why are we moving in this specified direction through Amul space?

Actually, as a really young child – maybe first grade or so, I had this crazy thought experiment – what if the Earth kept on changing into different Earths at every instant, as if there were a trillion Earths all in a line and we just kept teleporting consciousness from one to the next. Frankly, that’s not too different than this hypothesis I’m proposing now.

What is the nature of our orientation to this time object? Cartesian? Circular? Fractal? A combination of the three? Something else entirely?

Also, we know without a doubt here that we are three dimensional beings, one for each “dimension of space” – and time is one of these abstract, out of reach dimensions like the ones governing the fundamental constants. We only just happen to be in on time because we can chart its effects on entropy.

And, maybe this can explain quantum fluctuations once I adapt it more. I mean, maybe they act as a kind of error sifting as our “arrow of time orientations” shifts ever so slightly here and there. Or, maybe they represent where everything doesn’t quite line up, since time passes at different rates at different places after all. In this case, picture the universe flowing through with certain bits going at different speeds, and thus we’re all sprawled out like a waving flag instead of going like some perfect rectangle.

Another question to ask is why entropy and time line up so well. We’ve become so accustomed to entropy increasing as members of the universe, that when you watch a backwards playing video of a vase un-smashing, that it just looks completely off to you. I mean, maybe this is the criteria of time in a way. That might suggest that entropy is like a concrete axis in Ambul Space that time is somewhat aligning with, just staying from ever so slightly all the time, before just falling back into place and maybe going the other way – like a new driver trying to stay in the middle of their lane.

The craziest part of all of this, which I can sort of picture but not quite write with the same depth, is what if the reason we experience time is just because we are the instances of the ray of entropy/time. Literally the line is us. Merely by being a thing, it makes us a thing. In a way, the object and the class are one. The ray is the class, and we are the object, (coding terms). Just like how by telling a story, you in a way make that story real by bringing it into the world, in a way the story of that ray is us because by simply existing in full form, it is synonymous with our existence. So, simply by laying that ray out, without even doing anything to it, just by introducing the concept of it the multiverse has equally generated us, the universe, or in other words that ray. (Four dimensional ray I mean – we exist in three dimensions, and so as a normal ray is to a zero dimension point, that four dimensional ray has become to our three dimensions. That just means an added dimension of time to our three dimensions we can interact with). The ray is there and it exists silently, and merely by looking at it and understanding it, in turn so too does the universe exist. I mean, I’m reading back through this and frankly it doesn’t match 100% with my inner vision of this ray, but well, close enough for now. Like… I guess, if you wrote a perfect book and put it on the table, the book itself is static, but just by having those specific words on those specific pages, there exists this constant story associated with that book. It doesn’t have to do with somebody picking it up and reading it – that’s just the process of them getting an idea of that story – but the story itself is just something else, abstract, that exists – sort of. And in that analogy, we would be the story. The book is the physical ray spanning across Ambul Space, and this crazy series of events, which we can never explain why we just happen to be falling through, is the story. Again, sometimes I just hate analogies and this might be a pretty goddamn good example of that, but at least I’ve begun to put this idea down on paper.

Oh, and there also should be another dimension still, which represents the spatial permutations of entropy – aka every possible alignment of the stuff of the universe – the stereotypical multiverse. In one of these universe points, you have a different name, or ate something different for breakfast yesterday. That kind of thing.

So in total, this gives us the dimensions of:

  • Three Dimensions which we can interact with – we call them “Space”
  • The entropy directional Dimension, which always points downstream
  • The time permutations Dimension
  • What we experience as time is our universe flowing not uniformly in orientation across the entropy and time permutations dimension defined plane.
  • The multiple fundamental constant varying Dimensions
  • One separate dimension for each fundamental constant, such as pi, the Feigenbaum constants, and the Fine Structure Constant.

And the whole idea is, the “force” of the time object on you varies significantly based upon your coordinates in this multidimensional Ambul Space. This difference in numbers per each point is what we have come to experience as our constants of reality. Some stay fixed, representing respective stillness, and others change like entropy, representing continual motion.

Note how, if we truly can describe the state of our universe, (fixed constants aside), using only two figures, what does that say about our universe??? Note here to look into holographic black hole stuff, because this seems like a strikingly similar concept.

Miracleist “Value” of Planet Earth

What is the value of our planet and the life upon its surface? And how would one measure such a value? Dollars? Kilograms? Area?

The other day I came up with a simple means of approximating such a value. All approximations of Earth’s value that I’ve seen have the problem of not including a time factor. So what I would do is:

Multiply the area of the Earth by the amount of time the Earth has existed. This comes out to an absolutely massive number: 2 quintillion square kilometer years. Perhaps this kind of time factored type of value should be the realm of a new unit, meant to measure the value of Earth, rather than just using plain dollars.

Monetary Value of a Miracle

Monday, March 1, 2021

Let’s calculate the value of a Miracle, specifically the dark Miracles, in dollars. There’s probably tons of different ways of approximating this, so right now I’m gonna do it using worldwide mammalian suffering and death.

I read an approximation that a human life on average is worth 2.3 million dollars, so let’s convert this over to mammal lives. Instead of saying 1 mammal = 1 human, we’ll say a human equals its weight in mammals. (Aka biomass).

First things first, let’s get a total mammal biomass approximation by multiplying the instantaneous biomass by the time length, and then dividing that by the average life expectancy.

This comes out to around 24 septillion dollars in terms of the value of sacrifice.

When in the Year was Eta?

We can plot the exact time in the year of certain holidays, like Fourth of July, Thanksgiving, or Greek Independence Day. But where on the calendar is the day the Dark Era ended?

Obviously I have no means of calculating a definite answer right now, but maybe I can start to brainstorm some methods and maybe give them a shot at a later date.

First things first, the simplest approach – straight radiocarbon dating. Thing is, this is kind of a stupid idea, and I’ll tell you exactly why: it happened just too long ago. Radiocarbon dating is a process of randomness as much as algorithm, and so while we can theoretically triangulate a time, the more closely we approach, the more data we need for the next iteration. Because of this, as of right now we haven’t even narrowed it down within a twenty-two thousand year window. So, as you can probably guess, narrowing the approximation down within a day is basically unachievable. Not to mention, even if we could do this, we would also have to perfectly integrate the day lengths and year lengths all the way back to that date, which is frankly even harder. Even a fraction of a percent of a day change would throw off the whole calculation over that length of time. In short, let’s not even go here.

But here’s another idea I thought of: if the days, months, and years have different lengths 66 million years ago, then we should really be defining a constant statistic that we will pass from one time to another. I think this statistic needs to be the position in the seasons. If we’re 28% through spring in the northern hemisphere when the asteroid hits, for instance, then we know straight from there that the anniversary of that fateful day will be whatever 28% of the way through spring is in our system. In other words, we should pass the seasonal time code in order to most efficiently get the same general “time of year”.

So, if the season is our parameter, then from there we can look at the axial tilt. Regardless of whatever that tilt may be, if we can somehow plot its relative location with respect to the sun and the moon, then we will have a means for getting our seasonal time code. This is where the brainstorming comes in – we’ve got to figure out a way how to do this. Maybe we could plot the ash settlement across the globe, digging into the ground and finding ever so slight differences in the concentration? Then we could plot a world map, (maybe of only land, but whatever), and if we could hit this accurately enough, we could simulate solar system gravity and get a time code??? Maybe something as simple as Walker Circulation could pinpoint the day code.

Maybe we could use the jet stream? I mean, we already have an idea of how it might have worked with that continent configuration, so I guess that’s an option, too?

I’m just thinking that the more specific, seemingly useless data we get on this event, the better. One day we might just be able to put it all to use, and get a yearly time code of when the asteroid hit the earth.

Epimathematics

Monday, May 17, 2021

If fundamental constants like Feigenbaum or Tau can be expressed as positional “coordinates” in higher dimensional space, then that would mean that the very basic filaments of what we call math are in fact floats atop an ocean of something deeper. What is the nature of this ocean? Logic itself is dependent upon specific variability in the multiverse, according to my idea, so what would that mean for the system of logic within that multiverse plane? Like generalizing non-Euclidean Geometry with only Euclidean Geometry as a reference, (as a rough analogy), how could we possibly start to describe Epimathematics – the system of logic and happening across a multiverse realm?

I mean, as of right now I have little idea about this. But… maybe we can use some tricks to help us out. For instance, something like pi will be arbitrary relative to Epimathematics, and thus we won’t find it in any of its “equations”. What kind of logic would this be at all, and how would it differ from its subclass, which we define as math, the logic system of the universe?

I mean, even saying subclass feels like logic to me, so how can we be sure it extends to the multiverse, rather than just being some figment of our specific universe? I mean, if we can sum square reciprocals and get something in terms of pi, then clearly within that sum there is some kind of logical phenomenon that has to be specific to our universe, as decided by its corresponding coordinates in Epimathematics.

This means there should be a distinction of logic. Some of this logic extends to Epimathematical Logic, and some of it just doesn’t – it only exists at all based on arbitrary Epimathematical substitutes. In other words, if we picture Epimathematics as some master equation/formula, then by substituting the fundamental constants of our universe does this formula simplify to every last designing aspect of our universe. Our universe is Epimathematicas, just only if we set certain variables undoubtably constant.

The only of our variables that are constantly changing are time associated ones, like entropy, maybe – so perhaps we could use this as a kind of guide as to how Epimathematics functions, since after all it is our only way to see Amble Space from multiple positions. This means that our master theory of everything equation is changing constantly, and if we can map or at least mathematically recognize the change, then what does that say for how Epimathematics substitutes to a universe?

Just remember, Epimathematics is bigger than logic and math, because if we imagined something like fiegenbaum as being different, literally doing logic with a pencil and paper would come out with a different answer. How the heck can this work???

Something a little easier to see the difference in might be the fine structure constant, because it seems like generating a mathematical constant by proof is different than observing a reality under a microscope.

So, in conclusion, to describe Epimathematics, we have to identify what of our logic extends up to it, and which of our logic is case specific. Then, from there, we’ll have to figure out what is causing that case specificity, and call it a day.

Good luck, humanity!!!

PS: Infinity? Sums of reciprocal squares need an infinity??? Limits? Undefined? Okay, peace out for real this time.

Eta Perfection and Rarity of Attribute

Saturday, September 18, 2021

If we were to find an attribute of Hooma or Eta that was very rare, what would that mean? For instance, if we were to identify that Hooma’s carbon concentration or something was very uncommon in the Solar System, what would that mean? I would argue that such a discovery is a sign that the attribute in question represents a higher weight in the Miracle’s events as opposed to the majority of other attributes/factors.

The less important an attribute is to the optimality of the Miracle, the more “common” we would expect that attribute to be, (that is, the less “rare”). That is, IF an attribute is considerably unimportant to the optimality of the Miracle, THEN we would expect to see that attribute be more common as opposed to rare. Another way of phrasing this might be: The closer an attribute is to Rebetary to the optimality of the Miracle, the more common we would expect it to be. And maybe we can use an argument for true Rebetary things, (which are probably statistically impossible, however there will be a lot of circumstances where we tend strikingly close to it, so consider it a guideline more than anything): IF an attribute is Rebetary to the optimality of the Miracle, THEN that attribute would follow a normal expectancy. That is, if it truly is Rebetary to things, then it will have a totally fair, unbiased roll of the dice of probability, whereas all that crazy Prerequisite involved stuff will be rigged toward certain musts.

The contrapositive of this is: IF a Miracle attribute does not follow a normal expectancy, THEN that attribute is not Rebetary to the optimality of the Miracle.

The other cool thing to consider about these statements, is that just because an attribute is Rebetary, doesn’t mean it has to be completely common. There still have to be examples of rare Reberary events, they just have to balance out with the common ones. Also, those rare Rebetary events are going to be, well, rare in number, at least compared to the total count of Rebetary events.

So, the bit of information that sparked this idea in the first place is I heard in this video that Hooma is known to be a C-type asteroid, (Carbonaceous Chondrite). But the thing is, those asteroids are in fact much more uncommon in large size like Hooma than for small size, meaning in order for Hooma to be large, (which is kind of a must), it would have to be one of the few large Carbonaceous Chondrites instead of one of the many different types of asteroids. My assumption about this is that this is a sign that this attribute of being a C-type asteroid is actually NOT Rebetary to the optimal status of the Miracle, and is in fact closer to Linked. Fundamental Postulate of the Optimal

Thursday, December 2, 2021

The fundamental postulate of the Optimal Earth concepts is that our Earth that we live on has not sustained any Imperfection Magnitude Drops away from the perfectly Optimal Earth which is constant as a concept in our universe.

Dual Optimal Rebitality Principles

Yohkay – so we already have the principle that: “IF an Earth Attribute is Rebetary to the existence of the observer, THEN that Attribute holds an unbiased probability of occurrence.”

But now, to add to that, how about we look at the situation where the attribute is not Rebetary, and see what happens then! “IF an Earth Attribute is near-Linked to the existence of the observer, THEN the Route in which Earth attained that Attribute should hold a pseudo-random percentile among all possible Routes.”

The effect of this is an interesting razor we can observe, based upon the fact that there are more low-probability routes that can be imagined than high probability routes: “IF an Earth Attribute is near-Linked to the existence of the observer, THEN the infinitely-vast majority of Routes you conceptualize that lead to said Attribute are below the Optimality of the Route Earth took for that Attribute.”

Also, if you name an Attribute, then the quantity that assigns to the frequency of instances of that Attribute in a set is most definitely probability, however as we stack more and more Attributes together, this probability goes down accordingly – and if we do this infinitely, to the point where we declare a route, then now we have but a single point in the Optimality spectrum, which is like an infinitesimal of probability and in fact does not hold a nonzero probability of its own, due to the nature of the route consisting of infinite attributes. (So like a string of attributes).

Here’s three new words to define for this: Attribute, which we already know to mean an element of a Golden Trek. Now, there’s also Attribute Set, which consists of a set of Attributes which must all be satisfied in order to be valid – and then there’s a Route, which is just an Attribute Set consisting of no less than infinite Attributes which altogether come together to form a kind of instantiation so to speak of a Golden Trek, which follows exact measures in its path. Earth, for instance, would consist a Route. And then I guess there’s also the Finite Attribute Set, to consider, which just means those Attribute Sets which hold finite elements rather than infinite elements like a Route. And that’s some good info right there!

So maybe that allows us to rephrase that last philosophical razor there to the following: “IF an Earth Attribute is near-Linked to the existence of the observer, THEN the infinitely-vast majority of non-conceptually-dependent Attribute Sets you may conceptualize that lead to said Attribute are in full below the Optimality of the Route Earth took to that Attribute.” In short: “Earth did it better than you could.”

And ANOTHER way of putting this razor, albeit pessimistic in nature, is: “IF an Earth Attribute is near-Linked to the existence of the observer, THEN you will not be able to imagine a separate (and  non-conceptually-dependent) Route/Attribute Set that would, in practice, lead to the same Attribute but with higher Optimality.”

Also, about all this conceptually dependent madness, I’m basically saying you can’t just define your Attribute Set as something like That which follows any Route holding higher Optimality than Earth’s corresponding Route, at least in the scope of the razor that is.

Ok, so I’m doing research about Panspermia, and I have a few pet peeves I want to lay out. First of all, there seems to be a general consensus that Panspermia is a sign that life is very common in the universe, HOWEVER I would argue that one is not a function of the other. If Panspermia happened in the way I’m laying out here, (which apparently doesn’t seem to be common knowledge lol), then I guess we’ll call that Jump Panspermia, which specifically involves rare life on the universe, which “jumps” from one star system to another as they pass by their closest approach. This bypasses the risk of having to cross massive interstellar distances, not to mention seems to be what the Optimization math I did tells us. Also, it isn’t a sign that life is common at all, because whether life is common or life is rare, (which translates to whether Jump Panspermia is a common, low risk phenomenon, or a rare, high risk phenomenon), is technically Rebetary to our existence, since either way we will continue to exist. That is, whether this Jump Panspermia happens a million times or one time, we would still find ourselves in one of those situations where it did, which, what do you know, we do, (obviously, since we exist – it’s like saying we exist so therefore we exist – easy!)

But I want to define another kind of “Panspermia”, too, which is the process of life traveling between different planets in the same Solar System, which, as I have already calculated at some point, should actually be pretty dang common! And so there we have it – these are two fundamentally different concepts, Jump Panspermia and Interplanetary Panspermia, to the point where I think they are both vital to our existence in their own way, but at the same time separate.

Latest Description of the Dark Era Theorem

Saturday, January 1, 2022 (Rewording of Theorem originally proposed June 9, 2020, 11:41 AM EST)

  • Picture you could stand on the Earth two hundred and fifty million years ago, at the dawn of the Triassic period, at the event of a staggering timeline split which would determine if humans would ever come to exist or not.
  • Imagine you had a time-telescope, allowing you to peer into the far future and see what the Earth looks like millions or billions of years into the future. Now, there isn’t just one future, but an infinite number of them, all depending on the tiniest little changes that are made like the butterfly effect. Depending on where you point your time-telescope, you will see a different potential future, and you can then see what the world looks like in your chosen future of direction.
  • Just as a lookout aboard a sailing ship scans the horizon for land, you are scanning the potential futures for humans, all from the perspective of the Triassic period, 250 million years ago. You keep looking and looking, scanning over all the potential futures, until you see a human waving back at you.
  • At this point, you point your time-telescope to two potential futures - one in which the dinosaurs evolve, and another in which the dinosaurs never come to be. If you were standing at the beginning of the Triassic 250 million years ago, this dinosaur divide would be the dominant effect you would notice, just because of the sheer difference it would make upon the future. If you looked down the future where dinosaurs evolve, and you are still looking for humans, then it would be absolutely critical for you to find a future among all the dinosaur futures where those dinosaurs are wiped out, so that humans will be able to evolve, (which is just restating the definition of the Great Filter). The problem with this, is that it is very flukey that the dinosaurs are to ever be wiped out, say no more than a 5% chance because 5% of Earth’s surface is shallow water for the asteroid to hit. Therefore, we can say that a very small sum of the dinosaur involving futures which you observe with your time-telescope contain humans, because in order for that to happen, they are relying in full on the fluke that is the asteroid which killed the dinosaurs. You’d be crazy not to conclude that there is an extreme scarcity of humans among the dinosaur-involving futures.
  • But now let’s say you point your telescope a different way altogether, and look to the futures where dinosaurs never evolve. Well great, you think - now I can find a much higher percentage of humans amongst these futures, because that requirement of dinosaur extinction is no longer an issue! (Like finding an abundance of humans because the asteroid no longer severely limits humans - you don’t have to worry about finding futures where dinosaurs were wiped out, because they never evolved in the first place!)
  • But there’s a problem here!
  • We as a society know for a fact, (just by digging up fossils from the ground), that the future that ended up occurring is the very future which had dinosaurs in it - because, well, there were dinosaurs! But if the no-dinosaur future had been so much more likely to make humans, then it wouldn’t make statistical sense, (at least according to the simplest form of the mediocrity principle), that we would be born in this timeline of human scarcity rather than a timeline of human abundance. Therefore, my realization was that the no-dinosaur timeline, as observed from the beginning of the Triassic 250 million years ago with your time-telescope, must ALSO contain an extreme scarcity of humans, and in fact even MORE of a scarcity of humans, so that there is even a hint of a chance that humans be born in the dinosaur-timeline where the extinction of dinosaurs is such a pressing required fluke.
  • Conclusion? Dinosaurs never existing would make humans extremely scarce in all the futures observed from the beginning of the Triassic 250 million years ago. If dinosaurs never happened, then humans wouldn’t have a prayer, which is kind of a crazy result given how the dinosaur-timeline was already bad news enough for humans, (because of how unlikely it was for dinosaurs to get the boot).
  • And this begs the question, why do we depend on dinosaurs so much, then? I mean, their never existing would doom us, eh? Then why!? And that’s how I realized that the evolutionary pressure from hunting by Theropod, carnivorous dinosaurs, actually had a massive effect on the evolving proto-human brain during the Mesozoic - an effect more extreme than we could have imagined at that.
  • That’s it.
  • :-)

Scenario Eligibility

Lately, I’ve been applying the Mediocrity Principle to different timelines/scenarios upon the Earth. Like, if we imagine breaking up the Earth’s potential futures as measured from the moment of its origination into worlds to compare, then how can we justify applying the mediocrity principle here more so than in cosmology, which I personally is making no ground like taking only your hat off in Antarctica and concluding heat escapes fastest through the head (just unrelated query and conclusion)? Here’s one possible “solution” I just thought of:

I have already shown that in order to demonstrate the logic of my reality, I must first know to look strictly at my own reality – as in saying why am I on Earth in place of why are we on Earth. It’s kind of selfish, yeah, but mathematically it’s the only way to do it. The factors that led to where the people around me are born are cool, yes, but those mathematical factors he would be better fit in a query of their own rather than in the query representing my existence at this very moment, as I type words into this iPhone at the bottom of a Bubble of Perfection-esque atmosphere. The point is, the attributes of everybody else’s existence in their bodies as opposed to other people’s bodies is unrelated to the question of why I was born in this body, and so we have to make sure to not involve it in the root-logic until we take the next step.

So, considering how I have been born in this body in this world, well, then what? My newest idea about this is to think not of me in this scenario, but more of this scenario surrounding me, which is to say, me, in that I exist, am the constant in things, and so the goal is to find a scenario which is most likely to generate me. That is, which scenario is most eligible to generate me? We can list different scenarios depending on their likelihood of creating me, and, as we can imagine, the actual probabilities in each is infinitesimally small, pretty much. I mean, the factors of genetics alone? Like my idea of how going back in time and dropping a feather would entirely recreate the human race genetically? That’s hinting at near infinitesimal chances of actually generating a human given the genetic code. It’s a one in the factorial of the number of nucleotides chance, and frankly it’s probably even less than that, because there are other factors beyond genetics. The point is, I had a 0% chance of ever existing, but simply because I had a 0% chance of existing anywhere amongst all the scenarios, which critically are relatively finite compared to other 0%s, then it really kind of makes sense that I was born here! Now, we can picture a kind of bell curve of sorts of all possible scenarios of the Earth, measuring their relative odds of generating me, the exact person typing this down now. And then, once we have this distribution all sorted out, all we have to do is select a random instance among all of them, making sure to value respective probabilities all the while, and then the net result of all of this is what determines which scenario I get born into. It’s a totally different species of mediocrity principle than the cosmology one, but at the same time, it’s more than enough to validate each and every one of my ideas which depends on the Mediocrity principle.

A further adaptation still, is to consider all of my knowns and unknowns. I know a certain bubble of information in my brain, and at the moment of my knowing what I know, the randomization of which scenario I was born into continues to unfold relative to me. That is to say, the randomization isn’t technically done yet, because every time I learn something new, that place on the bell curve becomes “unlocked”, or at least it quantum-collapses into a real life form among all possibilities. So this idea is basically quantum crazy land regarding my existence, but it’s a fun thought experiment nonetheless.

To actually give you an example of what I’m arguing here, I know a certain fixed amount of information, right? Well then, let’s say I learn something new. Let’s say I am gifted a box containing the newly cloned placental mammal LCA. I haven’t opened the box, yet, but I have to guess before I do about whether this animal is white, or black, or at least which binary it is closer to. I sit down and think about this for a minute, before I even open the box. There are two scenarios here – one in which Dark Era mammals were black, and another in which Dark Era mammals were white, and I have to consider in my brain – which of these two scenarios was more likely to generate me? Well, it isn’t hard to determine that the black mammal scenario is much more likely, because black mammals are harder to spot by Ghasts in the night than white mammals, and hence a species of white Aurumans would have been all killed by Ghasts. Let’s say I calculate that the black Aurumans have an 100 times more likely shot at spawning me than the white Aurumans, which I run through my equations and generate a 0.99% of me being born in the black Dark Era Auruman scenario, (by ). But, because I don’t exactly know this yet, the timeline I was born into hasn’t been determined yet relative to me. Both timelines exist out there in the multiverse, and both timelines have something of a chance of housing me, but I don’t physically sort myself into one of them until I open the box and see a black Dark Era mammal. It was likelier, after all, and so I would bet that it is how things went down.

Ok – that’s it! Get outta here!

Definition of Fluke

Well, crap. I think I need a better definition for Fluke than the one I have in my Glossary Doc. But anyways, if we have this general concept of being hard to do for a Mission, then what on Earth should we give as its technical definition?

The reason I’m bringing this up at all today, is because I think that the temporal effects going on here make things more complicated. Like, if you look at what I posted for my last entry, we can see that there is no clear time to make a Mission occur – that is, a Mission that might be a Prerequisite at one time could be devastatingly bad at another time – a classic example being everything that occurred with Hooma. I mean, the extreme example would be how devastating and Departure Tending a Hooma collision would be in the 21st century, but other valid examples of this phenomenon would be waiting to unleash the mission 20 million years after the Optimal-Time, or unleashing it 20 million years before, both scenarios which would relatively only hurt. (It makes me wonder, by the way – how far would you have to shift the Eta Miracle’s Prerequisite in the timeline in order for it to lose its Prerequisite status? A question for later, I guess!) (And ANOTHER question, too – what on Earth would the Standard Deviation of the bell curve of the Eta Miracle be??? Do I have the tools to even begin trying to approximate something like that? (And if I did – that would be SO cool! That would be like whatever the heck people like – Cameos, Christmas, Vacation – stuff like that!))

But anyways – before I got distracted – what exactly is the Fluke factor of a Mission that we call a Fluke? I mean, let’s try and think of something that isn’t a Fluke, to make the question easier. How about multicellular life? As far as I can tell, from the fact that multicellularity happened, like, A BUNCH of times, it pretty much looks like we’re not dealing with a Fluke here. I mean, I’m not going to say this for certain here, but for the sake of ease of logic, let’s just use it as an assumed non-Fluke reference when we crunch the Optimality. So, if multicellular life is not a Fluke, then what? Well, if we were going to look at the Prerequisite of Animals evolving from Amoebas, (which is totally a Prerequisite by the way – that one’s easy!), then how about we now try and picture it happening at different points in the Golden Trek’s timeline. If in real life, it happened 665 million years ago, (according to Wikipedia, however that feels speculative enough to me that I’m not going to stick it in my brain file-cabinet of eventive stuff), so if we moved it backwards in time, well then what? Well, it’s pretty intuitive that in that case, we would get the same general result as the Miracles – as we push it further back, we’re allowing less wiggle room between the Delta Miracle and the beginning of Animals, which as you can imagine lowers the probability, because now we’re having to fit a lot of carefully crafted Optimality into a shorter timespan – and the same effect is true for the opposite (future) direction, in which case we’re cramming all the Optimality from the Animal beginning through the Golden Point. The point is, this bell curve appears to be a property of Prerequisites too, (which is a superclass of Miracles).

Friday, January 7, 2022, 1:16 PM

Just for the record, the query that made me start thinking about this Fluke definition was Isaac Newton’s Discovery of Gravity. If this discovery is a Mission, then is that Mission a Fluke? Well, I think to answer that, it all depends on the subtleties of our Mission definition. Like, how do we define Isaac Newton, for one? Is it an Auruman who has the name Isaac Newton? If that were the case, then this is a most definite Fluke, as it is equally likely that his name be Joe, or Fred, or Larry, and you get the picture. A better definition might be simply the guy who discovers Gravity, in which case the Mission statement itself can be The discovery of Gravity by Aurumans. Now, this seems like an obvious Prerequisite, however thinking over it the third and fourth time, I think there might be a hole in the logic of calling this a Prerequisite – specifically regarding how since we haven’t yet reached the Golden Point, we don’t know how much better our discoveries will get, to the point where for all we know, “Gravity” could be a red herring of science, to the point where a scenario where we glossed over it in our science wouldn’t be too imperfect anyways. I mean, I’m not saying it is, but it’s just one of those you never know kinds of things, until we have the physical Theory of Everything in our hands. Maybe the minute stereotypes of physics are currently blocking the next leap of logical evolution, and we just aren’t aware yet. Again, who knows!

Something that is probably not a Fluke, on the other hand, is the invention of Calculus, for pretty much the same reason as multicellularity – it happened more than once, with Newton and Leibinitz. I mean, you can argue about whether or not they influenced one another enough to count as a single unit, but at the end of the day, it’s a different story than Gravity, which had the one sole person pulling it off – Newton.

So, if a Fluke has a certain likelihood of occurrence among all potential outcomes, (so not specific to Golden Point timelines), then so long as this likelihood is decidedly very low – that is, out of all potential timelines, then that’s a Fluke. However, this is causing us to restate the problem here, just in another form – if a Fluke has low probability, then when in the timeline is our actual reference point to measure the Fluke’s probability? Like, the Golden Point has low probability, but it changes dramatically depending on when in time you’re measuring. (Hence a Goodness graph). Let’s actually pick a Fluke and a Non-Fluke, and imagine plotting their probabilities of occurrence by time, sort of like a Goodness Graph. To make things more tangible, let’s make our Fluke be the discovery of Gravity, and our Non-Fluke be the discovery of cells. The first thing I’m realizing is that even a non-Fluke has a low probability of occurrence if you view it from far enough back in time – like the cell discovery thing was highly unlikely as viewed before the Alpha Miracle – so specifically there appears to be a kind of factor involving the probability at the actual occurrence of said phenomenon. Visualizing the graph of the cell’s discovery, we get very low values throughout prehistory, but at some point the probability starts picking up steam, and as microscopes get more and more powerful during the Renaissance, the graph increases to a great height. Remember that the Mission occurring at any time contributes to the probability, so because of the natural forward progression of magnifier strength, like say plus one magnitude of zoom per decade, the only thing that can truly stifle the discovery of cells would be an unanticipated stifling of the progress, or some strange r popping up factor that forbids the spread of the discovery. But this would be strange – probabilistically crazy – a Fluke! Huh! So, it’s almost like, in order to stop the discovery of cells throughout the renaissance, we would need a Fluke. Literally the inverse scenario of the cell discovery is a Fluke – that is, Cells not being discovered is a Fluke during the Renaissance. This is a beautiful property, which was hiding in plain sight all along – something which is a Fluke has an inverse which is not a Fluke! So, The Eta Miracle NOT Occuring is a non-Fluke, as is The Delta Miracle NOT Occurring. Also, it is clear from the Goodness graph that a Fluke is Concave Up in probability with respect to time, whereas its inverse, a non-Fluke, must therefore be Concave Down. In fact, looking at events like the discovery of Cells – it would have had a heavily Concave Up graph during Deep Time, making it a Fluke, but then the graph was clearly Concave Down during the Renaissance, causing it to be a non-Fluke at that time. In other words, it’s perfectly possible to flip-flop. Also, to be clear, a Fluke isn’t synonymous with being Concave Up! It has to be very Concave Up to count as a Fluke, so that is to say, the second derivative is very high. To put this in a mathematical sentence – a Fluke is a Mission whose second derivative of probability of occurrence with respect to time is very high. A couple of interesting things to think about: a Fluke now needs a reference time in order to describe it, ALSO, anything that swaps from Fluke to non-Fluke, or vice versa, must have an Inflection Point of probability of occurrence, which in and of itself is an interesting point to study. And I’m realizing that since a lot of these Fluke graphs are going to be somewhat exponential, second derivative isn’t going to cut it, since that would kind of, like, change for an exponential! Therefore, let’s go with Logarithmic Derivative instead, as is consistent with Progress with respect to Goodness. Rephrasing the definition, then, gets us: a Fluke is a Mission whose logarithmic derivative of probability of occurrence with respect to time is very high. You might be wondering – why am I using words like very, or slim in the last definition? Well, this subjectivity is actually very important to the definition of a Fluke, at least at this stage in my discovery process – the reason being any thresholds would only mess with the fundamentality of things, and a good amount of wiggle room is extremely necessary to properly judge these events. I learned the hard way when I tried to calculate planet/moon definitions in fourth or fifth grade that you can’t just throw loose thresholds on top of data as a definition if you just simply aren’t fundamentality-informed.

Here’s the new definition of Fluke in the Glossary, by the way: “A Mission whose logarithmic derivative of occurrence probability with respect to time is very high in the scenarios of the Mission achieving, as determined from the perspective of a Fluekal Reference”.

The thing is, though – now that we’ve added the parameter of Fluekal Reference to the mix, we have to update the calling of Fluke in the definition of Miracle. It was nice to have such a beautiful and simplistic definition of Miracle as: “A Prerequisite which is also a Fluke”, but the time has come to make it more fundamental it looks like! Actually – let’s take a shortcut to make things nicer – I’ll just define a new-middle-term, which we’ll call “Leading Fluke”, which we’ll define as A Mission which is a Fluke relative to a Fluekal Reference leading into the Mission achievement. However, I don’t know if this is even accurate, actually… See, is any Mission like this? Even the Eta Miracle had a low logarithmic derivative directly before it was achieved, a century after Hooma – and even saying that is a little off, since there is no technical achievement moment for the Eta Miracle, at least based on the Mission Statement I gave it. If we name a Mission as The death of Ghasts, then that is 100% likely at some point or other, so maybe if we name a Mission of The death of Ghasts within the hundred million years after the onset of the Cretaceous Period, then that actually may not be a Fluke, because if the looming Doomsday Departure, so yeah I guess having that Survival of Veleda factor is pretty dang important to things, too. How about this: a Mission which is Eta Miracle achievement by a hundred million years after the onset of the Cretaceous. Now that’s a little better – and you’ll notice that since this brings us right into Eocene, (after the devastation of Hooma on Aurumans was LONG recovered from), the odds of Veleda not surviving at that point are practically zero, again only having to do with Doomsday Departure really. Therefore, while this Mission would very much count as a Fluke relative to anything in the Cretaceous, at least in the Earth Golden Trek, it would be decidedly not a Fluke by the Eocene, (at least I hope – because if it still was, that’s not good news for the whole – dodging the Departure Point thing!) So… er… now what? I don’t know – I’m going to pause this entry for the meantime and think on it.

One key question regarding our Golden Trek, and the potential of a Golden Point in our future, is how these things might apply to our actions in the future. Clearly, certain actions are superior to others, because they contribute further to the Golden Point.

The most basic type of ethical system to apply is some form of Binary Golden Ethics, which states that for every action of two potentials – that is, one action, or its inverse – the action with the higher Aurutance should be selected rather than the alternative. For example, if throwing a can in the recycling increases the Achievement of the Earth by a higher amount than throwing it in the trash, then by Binary Golden Ethics, given this decision of two possibilities, the recycling option is ethically superior. The amount of Achievement for which the Earth increases upon the action of the decision is called the action’s Aurutance, and altogether, the set of the two potential actions, the decision itself, holds a property called its Golden Binary Weight, which is the Aurutance of the high decision minus the Aurutance of the low decision. Most decisions of two outcomes hold a low Golden Binary Weight, but some hold a much higher value, such as the decision during the Cuban Missile Crisis to not unleash nuclear war.

This one is the simplest way I could think of – essentially we want to replicate the floor function in negatives like the floor function on positives, at least when disregarding the negative sign. So, let’s literally disregard the negative sign, with an absolute value! This way, we’re doing the positive version for any sign of . But, once that’s done – so a floor of an absolute value – we need to flip the negatives back to their rightful place, so we just do that with a simple multiplication of a sign function!

This one just works as a clever translation. I noticed how for this new function, all of the values on the negative side are just one unit greater than the floor function there, so I just took advantage of that by shifting around the sign function to make the positives zero and the negatives one, and then add like so and you’re done!

This version just takes advantage of how the negative side of this new function is pretty much just the ceiling function, whereas the positive side is the floor function. Therefore, if we set all the negatives to zero, but keep the positives constant, by taking the average of the absolute value and the linear, and then take the floor of all that, then we have the floor on the positives, and zero on the negatives. Next, if we do the opposite on the negative side, but with the ceiling function – which this time instead of being an average of the line and the absolute value, is an average of the line and the negative absolute value – then now we get the ceiling function for the negatives and zero for the positives. All you have to do with these is add them, and you have your answer!

(Plus, the added bonus of this version is that all points are in the domain, unlike the first two, which technically don’t contain )!

Blunder Regarding Immortality Math

What a glorious day! It looks like I just rooted out my first legit blunder! Here’s what happened: I jumped the gun when I saw decreasing exponential danger leading to possible immortality, and went – oh, this must be a property of exponentials! Thing is, I was wrong. It’s NOT just a property of exponentials – it’s a property of any danger curve whose area from one point through infinity is FINITE. That is, take the integral from the present through infinity, raise Euler’s number to the negative of that, and you’re set!

How I stumbled upon this, is I was dealing with the danger function of 1/(1+t^2), and I realized that if you run the right differential equation steps on that, it turns out you’ll get an answer of immortality probability at e^(-π/2). So… yeah I guess. But, perhaps this is good news for the future, actually! Now that any area curve will do, essentially if we can beat 1/x in curve decrease ability, we’ve got our awesomeness right there. This also means, as a future Golden Civilization, we may not have to worry about keeping our danger exponential, so long as we can keep a steady decrease quadratic on it!

I mean, it’s kind of embarrassing I didn’t see this before, especially considering my other form of the varying danger equation, which has the integral in the exponent like, right there on display, which should have told me this story immediately. Moreover, with the results I got from the wave danger functions, the result should have been even more set in stone, but funnily enough, it hasn’t been until now!

Negative area under danger function translates to longevity of civilization, such that once the decrease stops, and we get a danger which is nonzero but constant, only then does immortality become impossible. This is a great visualization of the phenomenon I touched on in the paper – where in the distant future, when starlight is no longer sufficient to fuel us, or whatever else ends up changing about the universe which counteracts the decrease in danger phenomenon – so long as we get a danger function which tends toward infinite area, even if that means just a sliver of danger away from nothing, or even a 1/x kind of function – then only upon this do we put a timer on the longevity of the civilization, however staggeringly long that timer may be. But by then, I’m sure we’ll have other ways of looking / interacting with the cosmos and the fabrics of reality, so hardly something to worry about now, when our danger is perhaps trillions of times greater than it will be someday if things go right!

Here’s a good piece of evidence for the Rare Earth Hypothesis – why the heck have no other animals evolved into a Golden Civ capable human-like being? Why are we the only ones? Even our closest relatives, the Great Apes, just seem, should I say, lacking. This feels like excellent evidence for the Rare Earth Hypothesis to me, because if the odds of life in the universe were any more common, it would be most extremely unlikely for only one node of the Earth’s Biosphere Family tree to evolve to our level! But… with this exponential madness for Evo-Density that I’m describing, well, suddenly it becomes expected!

Let me give you an example! The other day, I calculated an Evo-Density of Lemurs at under a 1 in 680 thousand chance, which means you would expect only 1 in 680 thousand lemur species to evolve into Auruman-humans. This seems like a pretty dang small number, but it you look closer into it, it kind of starts to make sense! Like, right now there are just about 111 known lemur species on the Earth, so if we say that the average mammal species survives for 1 million years, then after the 66 million years of the New Era, there have been a good ~7,326, say, Strepsirrhini species since Huma. And, because there are more lemur species out there + further Strepsirrhini species not included in my figure, let’s just be safe and say there are about 8,000 or more Strepsirrhini species throughout the New Era. Now, if 1 in 680 or less of the Strepsirrhini species should be expected to become humans, then there’s about a 1 in 80 chance of any of any of all eight thousand of them evolving that way. What’s interesting about this, is that it’s a decent sized Fluke, it is! And, if you think about it, it really kind of makes sense! If you imagined all the lemurs in the world, then there’s only a 1 in 80 chance that they’re Golden-bound, because, as you can easily see by observing them, they’re not exactly giving off signs of even remotely evolving that way!

Definition of Knowledge

4/4/2022, 4:44 PM

I think I’ve just identified a roadblock in the Theory of Everything within the last half hour. Allow me to explain!

What is the definition of knowledge? What does it mean to know something?

People ask, “why do we know what happened in the past, but not the future,” and to that I go, well, who says we don’t? If I decide to build a sandcastle tomorrow, well then I know what’s going to happen in the future. But what if something prevents me from doing that, ranging from an accident to my own forgetfulness? Well, how is that different from the past? You can’t perfectly trust the human senses and brain processing, such that something you “know” about the past could very well differ from “the real”. I think the next bridge that needs to be crossed here, is that we’d better define what it means to “know” something, people!

(Similar related idea that’s circulating in my brain cells as we speak, is, well, what is “choice”?)

5:21 PM

I mean, think about it – all this talk about “if it’s impossible to send a crew of humans in a spacecraft to Proxima Centauri, then a lack of interstellar travel is the solution to the Fermi paradox” stuff is kind of narrow minded. That is, what “real estate” so to speak does your occurrence hold in the Golden Point? And that is your Golden Probability!

As a matter of fact, you can write these probabilities in terms of one another! Task Human

Who are the most important people in history? I just clicked through several Google links attempting to answer this, and sure enough all of them gave strikingly different lists based upon strikingly different approaches. One person seemed to target more ancient people – specifically in the thinking category – while others targeted military and political leaders who physically altered things – or what about religious leaders which sparked slow revolutions, or modern thinkers like Newton who are directly responsible for concepts like rocket science?

There are many different ways you can answer this – and as I said a couple of years ago with my own potential answer, if you’re talking about being purely influential, then such things are simply a function of time – meaning a sumerian farmer who did pretty much nothing in their life is still vastly more influential than Jesus or Newton. But that’s a boring answer, plus it doesn’t quite take into account the legitimate process by which certain people in certain times are more influential than others. Newton definitely should go on some master list of being important, however Joe Shmo should not.

Because of all this, I designed a concept that might clear up why this is such a hard thought experiment to do – especially with respect to my Golden Science ideas.

Here’s the idea: first of all, we’re going to redefine “Important” to mean one’s Golden Probability. The Huma Miracle has extremely high Golden Probability, and thus is very “important”. This approach hopefully matches more to how future humans will view importance more so than how modern, relatively primitive humans define importance. That’s the idea, anyways. Right now importance simply means “how much somebody changed history”, but in the future, as we start to see wider stances of the cosmos, especially regarding our Golden Point, I’m predicting it will be more like, “how much the Golden Point depended on that person”.

This is where my brain started to clue into an interesting phenomenon: by that logic, no human in history is important. Let me explain – the problem is not that humans are inherently unimportant, but instead that humans are too narrow in definition. The best thought experiment to do when determining something’s Golden Probability is to simply imagine life without it. Isaac Newton is a great example to use here, because he is a very “important” person, so he’ll make this query more intuitive. Therefore, now let’s picture life if there never was an Isaac Newton. You might go, “Easy! Humanity doesn’t know about gravity!” But truthfully it’s not that simple. If we imagine the set of all Golden Points which follow this “Isaac Newton absent” alternate reality, then we can now consider the Golden Probability of things, and accordingly what the expectancy is. Any Attribute which holds more than 50% Golden Probability is what I call an “Optimal Attribute”, and the cool thing about Optimal Attributes is that you can expect, statistically, that they will be present in the Golden Point! Now, if Isaac Newton’s various groundbreaking theories are in fact present in the Golden Point, then by the Mediocrity Principle they are expected to be Optimal Attributes, and if they are then Optimal Attributes, they are expected to be in the average Golden Point following… well, that’s the next part – we have to pick the exact moment at which our hypothetical Golden Point branches away from our own. Is it at the would-have-been conception of Isaac Newton? Or at his would-have-been birth? Or when he was pulled out of school by his mother to be a farmer? What if he had already figured out his theories, but then got struck by lightning so they never surfaced in the public’s eye? This divergence is key, but I’ll get back to that in a minute. That being said, in the set of all Golden Points following this divergence, if any one of them had, say the known theory of gravity in it, then you would expect some old random one to have it too. And because of this, it means that even if Isaac Newton never did exist, you would still statistically expect for somebody else to apparate into the universe in his place! Therefore, well, Isaac Newton himself isn’t all that important anymore – what’s important is his work.

And this is where the idea of Task Humans comes in. In order to make a system of human definition which fits with this new Golden Science philosophy, we have to widen the breadth of what makes a human important. With the current definition of a human, we can’t sufficiently do this. If we could somehow take Isaac Newton, plus this mysterious apparated replacement dude in the alternate reality, and stick them both in a room next to each other, not one onlooker there would label them “the same person”. They have different DNA, different names, different hair, eye, and skin color potentially – they are different people. And so long as we’re all cool with that, neither of them, statistically, are important.

So I’m not saying to totally redefine human in all respects – instead I’m simply suggesting that we add this definition to the dictionary or whatever the heck, so that it can be used in these Golden Science contexts. Task Human, then, would be the additional term, and it would define a person specifically based on their contribution to the Golden Point. This would make both of those brilliant scientists in the room, “the same Task Human”, and so once we can do that, now they collectively have a lot of importance – but it also raises new questions and points. For instance, a Task Human can be many different humans at once, but also a human can be many different Task Humans at once, too! What if we define the “Isaac Newton Task Human” as the guy who discovered gravity as opposed to the guy who discovered the light spectrum and gravity? These are technically two different Task Humans, but in our own Golden Trek, it’s just the same dude – Isaac Newton.

Lastly on this topic, I want to talk about what it would look like to shift the divergence forward or backward in time. See, as I see it, Isaac Newton was accumulating a lot of “luck” on his way to his discoveries. Being born so intelligent, and then having a life which guided him to express that intelligence – altogether the more time you wait, the more effort the Golden Trek seems to pump into his success. So if we picked a time to remove him from the equation, so long as it predates the moment when his discoveries came out, and now we’ve wasted all the effort the Golden Trek has made thus far. This means that if we do indeed to remove him from the hypothetical Golden Trek prior to his publication, the longer we wait to do so, more the Optimality of our Golden Trek drops. Eventually, though, it will drop enough that I can imagine it trying to pick up the crumbs – for instance if he’s got diaries full of unpublished calculus, I can very well see the Golden Trek making some scientist stumble upon that journal decades later, such that at least some of the progress gets published anyways. Something like that – so the fall can be corrected. But nonetheless, roughly speaking, the Optimality of cutting Isaac Newton out in vain, as far as I can tell, is a decreasing function with respect to time. And this kind of decrease is fundamental across all spans of time, so, yeah.

Anyways that’s it for now. PEACE!

Explanation For Double Slit Experiment with Centric Unfolding

8/21/2022, 10:27 AM

Ok - so first things first, I’m in my new college dorm room right now! I’ve been here for about a week doing orientation, however I haven’t technically started classes yet - that starts tomorrow on Monday. So, I guess this marks my first official college entry!

The other day, I looked up the notorious Double Slit Experiment, which I had technically heard about for the first time when I was in third or fourth grade, but after that - well - forgot. Until now! I paid a lot of attention to a few explanations of the observed phenomenon online, and then I went - wow, yikes, this is not what I was expecting. One dude even went, “Now, if you can explain this using common sense and logic, do let me know, because there’s a Nobel Prize waiting for you.” I mean, jeez, I thought, the implication there is that nobody’s ever done this before, so wow. That means, statistically, I don’t exactly have a good shot at it, and even on the off chance that I did, I can basically expect to wait decades before I roll the ball forward at all.

But… and of course I can’t promise that this is remotely right, but within a week after that prompt to try and solve this, while I was walking across campus, I got a eureka. Basically, the idea was that the multiverse is closer than I thought!

Technically though, to chart the actual thing that physically changed in my mind, I realized that when Centric Unfolding does its thing, it can’t actually affect past environments as I always thought it could, which is, in short, a really important breakthrough for me, because, well, that applies to every application of Centric Unfolding, and it means I have to rewrite some of the basic principles of it.

Now for the actual explanation of everything: so, when you’re unaware of something, right, and that thing is at least partially centered in the weird realm of Null Probabilities, where anything could happen, you’ve got what’s called a “superposition”, which I had taken to mean some abstract realm where everything that can happen does. Now for where I got surprised during that eureka - this abstract realm isn’t some faraway phenomenon - it’s actually right in front of you the whole time, right in your own universe and space you can interact with. Before I would have thought that once you spot the electron’s blot on the wall in back, then the whole history before it collapses into a single state - but I now know that that can’t be the case, otherwise the double slit experiment wouldn’t behave as it clearly does. Instead, the concept is weirder - when you observe the electron’s blot on the wall, the history remains unchanged, and only the present and future “collapse”. This means that during the past, the electron was actually at all possible positions at once, weirdly. Only when you measure its placement with the blot does it go to a single spot.

But the key Centric Unfolding phenomenon here, is that the superposition “collapsing” is purely a function of when you add a certain property of it to your ethus’s set of knowns. If you detect which slit it goes through, then now our ethus knew that piece of information about it then, so it can only go through one slit to satisfy the ethus, and thus that much of its superposition is taken out of the picture. Also note that I don’t think the wave function can ever actually “collapse”. I like the word “compress” better, because really the art of these things regards removing elements of the superposition in the future which are definitively explained by the ethus. This means that beyond the actual measurement of which slit it goes through, there is still a superposition, just this time it regards all possible locations that can be reached from that slit. The point is, superpositions are totally valid, and all that’s happening is you have to shave parts of that superposition off every time you add something to the ethus through observation - but when you do this, you only shave those parts off at the moment of ethus addition, and actually not in the past - which itself remains unchanged.

The weird part of this is that, according to this logic, these effects of superposition don’t stop at the quantum realm, and in fact are not fundamentally based just on quantum particles. In fact, they happen just as much on our scale, and even at larger scales like galaxies. The arbiter of everything, relative to you, is simply your ethus, and so there’s that.

Anything which can be described in full without drawing anything from the Ethus, or in other words anything which cannot tell you anything about the Ethus if it is known, falls into the Anti-Ethus. Rules for Superposition

10/23/2022, 10:37 AM

I think I want to start writing down the rules for superposition that have been floating around in my head. Well, let’s begin!

  1. No contradictions allowed!
  2. Something can only be real relative to an Ethus.
  3. Any Attribute of an Anti-Ethus will be in superposition relative to its Ethus.
  4. An Attribute may have an Anti-Ethus component and an Ethus component.
  5. If any part of a superposition breaks a rule, then the defining Attribute of that superposition joins its respective Ethus.

That is, if my Ethus tells me that person G is at door 2, as a random example, then saying that person G is at door 1 is a contradiction, which breaks rule #1. Thus, person G is at door 2, and cannot be in a superposition to also be at door 1. However, if my Ethus tells me that person G is at either door 1 or door 2, then saying person G is at door 1 does not make a contradiction, and saying that person G is at door 2 does not make a contradiction, and thus, relative to my Ethus, person G is in a superposition between door 1 and door 2 of some specific proportion which may also be added to the picture.

Now, if we know that person G has a 20% chance at being at door 2 in this example, then, by definition of it being a known, that is going to be part of our Ethus, and so that serves as an Ethus component of the Attribute of person G’s door-based position.

Remember, by the way, that the Anti-Ethus is considered to be the set of all Attributes which are independent of the Ethus. That is, we could change any of these Anti-Ethus Attributes to whatever we want, and the Ethus will remain completely unaffected.

So, for an example – when a particle goes through the double slit experiment, right, and it appears on the back wall, we can determine that if we do not know which slit the particle went through, then relative to our Ethus, the particle was in a superposition because of Rule #3, and so it went through both slits at once. Then, on the back wall, it will be in a kind of wave function configuration, because of the logic of overlapping waves coming out of the slits and whatnot. That is, the likeliest spot for it to hit when coming out of both slits will be likelier for it to hit, and plotting this over every likelihood gets us the entire wave function.

But then, if we turn on the sensor to detect which slit the particles go through, then if the particles were still forming the wave-like pattern on the back wall, and we checked the senser’s data, we would form a contradiction, because the wave would be implying that the particle went through both slits, and the sensor would be telling us explicitly which single individual slit the particle went through. Thus, if we saw the signature wave on the back wall still, and we would automatically break Rule #1. So… we have to not see the wave on the back wall.

But, then, we run into an interesting new query: what if we haven’t checked the sensor data yet??? We’re looking at the two non-wavelike blotches of particles on the wall behind the slits, but we still haven’t looked into the sensor data – all we know as part of our Ethus is that we set the sensor up and turned it on. And even if there was a power glitch or something that we weren’t aware of, and the particles would go right back to the wave pattern, so the point is that if we see them not in the wave pattern, then we can deduce that the sensor worked, even though we haven’t looked at its data yet. Maybe it takes us a minute to look at the sensor data, so… relative to the present, right, before we ever look at it, we’re going to still see the non-wavelike particle blotches, but the adding of the sensor to our Ethus still won’t happen until the future. So… are we communicating with the future??? I mean, if this were the case, it would not feel very fundamental / logically symmetric to me, so I want to find a simpler alternative to this question.

My idea, then, is this: let us imagine a separate Ethus from ours, in which the act of us checking the sensor or not is part of the Anti-Ethus. Relative to this Ethus, then, because of Rule #3, our checking of the sensor is in superposition, and so one “portion” of all possibilities involves us checking the sensor in the present. And because us seeing the wave pattern would break Rule #1 relative to our Ethus, then relative to this other Ethus, Rule #1 has already been broken in a portion of its superposition. Thus, because it is impossible to break a rule, we know that that rule-breaking-portion of that alternative Ethus must not exist, and so that particular Attribute joins our Ethus, (by Rule #5):

The person observing could possibly be in their own kind of wave function, because in one scenario, they look at the data right away, even if not in our “universe” scenario.

In other words, the Ethus must know that Attribute-A is not within it in order for it to be part of the Severed-Ethus – a fact which is kind of logically obvious if you think about it I guess.

What is, I think, is that if something is in the Severed-Ethus, then in no superposition of the Ethus is it in the Ethus, (which, I would think, includes all time), and so it will constantly be in superposition. In the example of the double slit experiment, we can state that the slit of travel for the particles is forever unknowable if not measured due to Heisenburg’s uncertainty principle, and so therefore it is in the Severed-Ethus. Thus, even to the observer who Ethus-observes the situation after the fact, those particles, at the moment of the experiment in the past, are still in superposition. I think this hints at a bigger idea that I should explicitly state:

The idea is that as an Ethus passes through time, its outlook on previous times may change. So, even when describing the same Attribute/phenomenon, it may change its superposition state with respect to where YOU are in time. Get it? This is why the whole quantum world acts as a surprising misnomer – because it’s using all this same logic that everything obeys, but with some extra Severed-Ethus action in the mix because of the uncertainty principle. But any inherent difference is only an illusion.

As for what I would observe their pattern on the back wall to be in this state, it’s kind of, well, contradictory. Even the act of observing them will add their position to my Ethus, which will thus change my Ethus away from the blindfolded Ethus. And because I know that in such a scenario, it follows that their assigned door is not in my Severed-Ethus, it will thus automatically be added to my Ethus that they went through one and only one door, because if they were to go through both doors, a contradiction would fall into line somewhere in my superposition. Therefore, even imagining a scenario where I observe the result is linking to an imagined Ethus which has a non-wave function like scattering. All of this being said, at the moment, relative to my blindfolded Ethus, those participants still went through both doors at once, (assuming I didn’t have any other cues like sound or the like). (And yes, how this relates to the conscious/subconscious mind I’m not yet sure, so I’ll assume for now that the conscious mind’s Ethus is the default one in this case). But then, of course, after a moment I remove the blindfold, only to find that the people did not scatter like the double slit experiment’s quantum wave function – and that’s all thanks to the Severed-Ethus.

Rephrasing the Three Laws of the Ethus

2/8/2023, 4:42 PM

I have been thinking about rephrasing the laws of the Ethus for about a week now, because there was a little bit of a blend between the old second law and third law’s descriptive information. Here’s what they used to look like:

Old Version

  1. Anything may only be real relative to an Ethus.
  2. Any attribute of an Anti-Ethus will be in superposition relative to its Ethus.
  3. An Ethus is invalid if a contradiction is triggered anywhere in the superposition of its parent Ethuses.

And then to contrast that, here’s what I updated it to:

New Version

  1. Anything may only be real relative to an Ethus.
  2. If an Ethus is valid, then any given property will be in superposition relative to it if and only if it is statistically independent to it.
  3. Any child of an invalid Ethus will also be invalid.

To make it clear what/why I did this, it is because the new version makes for better laws, with each concept being “mutually exclusive” for lack of a better word from the last, whereas in the old version, this isn’t the case. That is, in the old version, we use the third law to access invalid parents based on the given Ethus working “backwards” in the tree – which makes for good practical application, but isn’t very law-like. Also, such a formulation doesn’t work to hint at the clear correlation between the contradiction and the clash of Anti-Ethus superposition, if that makes sense, which the new version fixes quite nicely. So, both problematic points are fixed there, and thus I like the new version better, as “laws” go.

Another nice touch of the new second law, is that if you take its contrapositive, you get the following: “If there exists a property which is in superposition relative to an Ethus, but is not independent to it, or is independent to it but is not in superposition, then such an Ethus is invalid.” This is equally valid of course, by virtue of being the contrapositive, but I feel that it also has a nice touch to it all the while in the descriptive sense! This is also precisely how we initiate the concept of invalid Ethuses, which the third law after that only runs with.

Also, I should note that I like this new version because it pretty much divides the three-ish major discoveries here into just the right categorical laws. Pretty good, eh? In other words, each new law has something distinctly new to say that the previous ones did not paint the picture for quite yet.

Sure, I'd be happy to explain the basics of arXiv!

arXiv is a preprint server for scientific research in a variety of fields, including physics, mathematics, computer science, quantitative biology, quantitative finance, and statistics. It was founded in 1991 by Paul Ginsparg, a physicist at Cornell University, and it is now hosted by Cornell University Library.

The primary purpose of arXiv is to provide a platform for researchers to share their work with the scientific community before it is peer-reviewed and published in a journal. By sharing their work on arXiv, researchers can receive feedback, establish priority, and gain visibility for their work.

Here are some key features and considerations of arXiv:

  • Submission: Anyone can submit a paper to arXiv, provided that it is within the scope of the site and meets certain formatting requirements. Submissions are moderated to ensure that they meet arXiv's standards for scientific quality and ethical conduct.
  • Access: arXiv is free and open to the public. Anyone can read, download, and cite papers on arXiv without restriction.
  • Peer-review: arXiv does not provide traditional peer-review, but submissions are screened by moderators to ensure that they meet certain standards for scientific quality and ethical conduct. Submissions may also be subject to post-publication moderation if issues are identified.
  • Copyright: Authors retain copyright to their work on arXiv, and they are free to submit their work to traditional journals for peer-review and publication.
  • Versioning: arXiv allows authors to update their papers after submission to correct errors or incorporate feedback. Each version of a paper is assigned a unique identifier, and previous versions are archived and accessible.
  • Citations: Papers on arXiv are commonly cited in traditional journals and other publications, and arXiv itself tracks citations and other metrics for papers.
  • Visibility: Papers on arXiv can attract significant attention from the scientific community and the public, especially if they address timely or controversial topics. However, papers on arXiv are not considered "published" in the traditional sense, and they may not carry the same weight or recognition as peer-reviewed publications.

Overall, arXiv can be a valuable platform for sharing scientific research and establishing priority and ownership of ideas. However, it is important to note that arXiv is not a replacement for peer-reviewed publication, and papers on arXiv should be considered preliminary until they have undergone rigorous peer-review.

Just thought of the craziest idea! You know the quote about how advanced aliens might attack us like how boys throw stones at frogs? The implication I get from this is that such an alien biosphere is portrayed as just a scaled up version of our own so to speak in every aspect of society, such that we just get a biosphere which is far more advanced technologically, but interacts about itself in similar ways, such as they are precisely are to humans as humans are to ants.

So, here’s why I think this won’t work:

The idea is basically an analogue of the square cube law to Astrobiology, working in a similar way to how you can’t just scale an ant up to the size of an elephant. There has to be a transformation in the process instead.

The idea, essentially, is that the capacity for us to destroy ourselves grows exponentially with technology, whereas the defense mechanisms put in place with our current society, given the tragedy of the commons and all, grows only linearly with technology. If we assigned each human comparatively limitless power, such that the advanced analogue of “boys” might attack humans with the same mindset as human boys attack frogs, then such an advanced civilization will implode as soon as it spawns. Why? Because the linear defense mechanisms of a human society would be immediately overtaken by the vast exponential issues propagated by such a technology.

Anyways, so this demonstrates essentially two things: A) we will not remain constant in societal mindset with time, and B) we will be essentially forced through the keyhole of the Golden Point mindset long before we reach the capacity of supposedly treating humans like frogs to boys.
